thread:
Elena Voss: Heads up — Competitor Atlas just shipped a per-route automatic fallback toggle that downgrades to cheaper model variants when latency spikes. Sales flagged it as a demo highlight. ⚠️
Alex Kim: Saw that. UI is tiny but the defaults are aggressive — looks like they route by 95th percentile latency.
Maya Singh: Which customers asked for this? Are we seeing demand?
Elena Voss: Two enterprise pilots last week asked for simpler controls to limit spend during peak. They want an "auto-fallback" option that doesn't require per-request policy wiring.
R. Carter: Engineering note: we already support routing policies but UI + safe defaults is the missing piece. Big risk: if defaults are too lenient we could degrade quality.
Samira Ortiz: From CS: customers ask for "set-and-forget" cost protection. They don't want to manage rollout rules per model.
Alex Kim: Proposal sketch: add a per-route toggle in Console that enables fallback to a configured model tier (e.g., quality -> standard -> economy) and expose a safety window (min tokens preserved). Minimal backend: reuse existing routing graph + policy that checks latency and token budget.
Maya Singh: Required launch criteria (suggested):
- explicit consent checkbox in Console + audit log
- default policy = conservative (fallback only after 2x SLO breach)
- telemetry: sample requests flagged as fallback + side-by-side quality compare metrics
- e2e rollout with canary at 5% tenants
R. Carter: Implementation notes:
```
- Control plane: new route flag (auto_fallback_enabled)
- Runtime: subscribe to SLO monitor, emit fallback_decision event
- Metrics: fallback_rate, post_fallback_rejects, quality_regression_score
```
Elena Voss: Tradeoffs: faster to ship as an "opt-in toggle" for Beta vs. full automatic-on-by-default product that Atlas has. Leaning Beta first. Thoughts?
Alex Kim: Beta ok. We should push an initial spec that keeps quality observability front-and-center. If fallback_rate spikes, auto-disable for that tenant.
Maya Singh: Sales asks: timeline and messaging. If Beta in next sprint, we can offer pilots as "cost-safety" feature. Need one-liner and risks for sales playbook.
Samira Ortiz: I'll draft sales blurb. Also request a simple demo scenario: show cost saved during a synthetic surge without hurting SLA more than X%.
R. Carter: Tentative timeline: spike -> spec PR this week, infra stub next week, Console toggle + telemetry in 3 sprints, Beta rollout end of Q.
product-bot: New action created: product/auto-fallback/spec-review assigned to @Alex Kim, due 1776620000.
Elena Voss: Decision: go Beta (opt-in). Owners: Alex (spec/console), R. Carter (runtime), Maya (biz/sales comms), Samira (demo). Follow-ups: Alex please post a short spec + acceptance criteria by EOD Friday.
Alex Kim: On it. Will include acceptance criteria and a simple QA checklist. :thumbsup:
Maya Singh: I'll coordinate pilot list and messaging once spec is up.
thread_summary: Competitive signal: competitor shipped per-route auto-fallback. Team decides to build opt-in Beta with conservative defaults, telemetry, and sales demo. Owners assigned and spec due EOD Friday.
